ACME Ops: Hey, we're seeing the collector create the bundle but upload to our Azure blob keeps failing with 403. Request ID from our side: req_0a4b3c. Can someone help?
Maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact error from the collector logs and the presign/sas URL (or a redacted version)? Also which version of the private collector are you running?
ACME Ops: Collector v1.4.2. Error snippet from /var/log/redwood-collector.log: 

2026-02-22 14:05:12 ERROR upload: azure_upload.go:142: upload failed: Put "https://acmeprod.blob.core.windows.net/bundles/redwood-...": 403 Server failed to authenticate the request.
Request ID: 9a7f6bcd-0000-0000-0000-5f6e12345678
x-ms-request-id: 9a7f6bcd

We get the same when we try the presigned SAS URL in curl. We redacted the SAS token for chat.

curl -v "https://acmeprod.blob.core.windows.net/bundles/redwood-bundle.tar.gz?sv=...REDACTED..." -o /tmp/out.tar.gz
*   Trying 52.239.140.134...
* Connected to acmeprod.blob.core.windows.net port 443
> GET /bundles/redwood-bundle.tar.gz?sv=...REDACTED... HTTP/1.1
> Host: acmeprod.blob.core.windows.net
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*
>
< HTTP/1.1 403 This request is not authorized to perform this operation.

ACME Ops: Note we're behind a corporate proxy and we have strict SELinux policies. Collector runs as systemd service under user redwood.

Evan SRE: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) SELinux AVC denies often break the chunked upload helper (collector uses ms-rest-go/azure sdk). Check /var/log/audit/audit.log for avc: 

type=AVC msg=audit(167707...): avc:  denied  { write } for  pid=1234 comm=\"redwood-collector\" name=\"tmp\" dev=\"sda1\" ino=56789 scontext=system_u:system_r:unconfined_service_t tcontext=unconfined_u:object_r:tmp_t tclass=file

2) Proxy: Collector spawns a subprocess to do multipart PUTs. Make sure HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY are set for the service and allow CONNECT to port 443.

Priya Eng: Also asking whether redaction ran. We had one customer where emails still leaked because /var/log/audit.log was excluded by default redact policy. Can you confirm the bundle contents show PII? If so we'll need the bundle to repro.

ACME Ops: We saw a few emails in /var/log/secure inside the tarball. We don't want to upload the raw bundle to your S3/Blob — is there a way to hand it off securely?

Maya (Support): Yes — we can accept an encrypted bundle via scp to our temporary bastion, or you can upload to your blob and share a short-lived SAS (we'll only request specific paths). Two safe options:
- Generate the bundle with our redaction policy override locally (see command below) and then scp to support-bastion:2200
- If scp blocked, run the collector with --upload-backend=none and attach the bundle via the support secure upload flow (we'll provide an SFTP endpoint)

Maya (Support): To generate a redacted bundle locally (run on the private environment):

sudo /opt/redwood/collector/bin/collector \
  --collect-logs \
  --collect-config \
  --redact-policy /etc/redwood/custom_redact.json \
  --output /tmp/redwood-bundle-1765556789.tar.gz \
  --upload-backend=none

Make sure collector is v1.4.2+ so --redact-policy is supported. The custom_redact.json should include regexes for emails and IPs. Example add: 

{\n  \"redactions\": [\n    { \"type\": \"regex\", \"pattern\": \"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\" },\n    { \"type\": \"regex\", \"pattern\": \"\\\b\\\d{1,3}(?:\\\.|\\\d{1,3}){3}\\\b\" }\n  ]\n}

ACME Ops: Will try. Two follow-ups: 1) We can't lift SELinux long-term — any mitigation? 2) If SAS fails due to auth, could it be clock skew on the private host?

Evan SRE: For SELinux, prefer setting a targeted boolean or a file context rule rather than permissive: check audit2allow to generate a module, then test. Example flow: 

ausearch -m avc -ts recent | aureport -a
ausearch -m avc -ts recent | audit2allow -M redwood_collector_fix
sudo semodule -i redwood_collector_fix.pp

That avoids broad policy changes. Also ensure /opt/redwood/collector/tmp is labeled tmp_t if collector writes there.

Priya Eng: Clock skew is a common root cause for SAS auth failures. Check date -u and compare to NTP servers. Small skew (>5 minutes) can make SAS tokens invalid. Also validate the SAS token permissions (rw create write) and expiry window.

collector-bot: upload_attempt: bundle \"/tmp/redwood-bundle-1765556789.tar.gz\" -> backend azure (presign=redacted) status=403 err=\"Server failed to authenticate the request\" request_id=\"9a7f6bcd\"\n
ACME Ops: Ran the redaction locally and scp to bastion succeeded. We attached the bundle to the support ticket s12345 via secure transfer. Also ran date -u: our host was ~3 minutes behind. We corrected ntp and re-ran curl to the SAS and got 200 for a test GET. Trying collector upload now.

Maya (Support): Great — thanks for the bundle. We'll start an internal repro using the same collector version + SELinux AVC entries you sent. If you still get a 403 after NTP fix, please paste the exact collector startup environment (systemctl show -p EnvironmentFile, Journalctl lines) and the full request id from the failing attempt.

ACME Ops: Will do. For traceability, latest failing attempt request id: req_0a4b3c (same as first message). Attaching the short journalctl tail: 

-- journalctl -u redwood-collector -n 50 --no-pager --since \"2026-02-22 14:00\" --output=short
Feb 22 14:04:58 host systemd[1]: Started redwood collector service.
Feb 22 14:05:11 host redwood-collector[1234]: INFO starting upload to azure blob
Feb 22 14:05:12 host redwood-collector[1234]: ERROR upload: azure_upload.go:142: upload failed: 403 Server failed to authenticate the request. request_id=req_0a4b3c

Evan SRE: Perfect — that request_id and the NTP note are enough for us to repro. We'll run a local repro with a short-lived SAS and mimic the proxy + SELinux. Follow-ups: if you need a quick workaround, set --upload-backend=scp and scp to the bastion from the collector service user (ensure keys in /home/redwood/.ssh).

Maya (Support): I'll open an internal ticket with eng-runtime and eng-sre to validate SDK behavior under SELinux. Priya, marking for redaction policy review too. @Priya Eng can you own the redaction policy PR to include audit/secure logs by default?

Priya Eng: On it. I'll also add a FAQ note about NTP causing SAS 403s to our private deployment runbook.

ACME Ops: Thanks everyone — will update ticket s12345 after the next upload attempt.
